target_objects: job ow_tp_ingest_cnvingest (serverless notebook task, manual trigger, max_concurrent_runs=1)
golden_baseline_location: docs/tech-partnerships/recon/sftp_ingest_poll-cnvingest.golden.json (captured from a deterministic local run of the legacy ksh job: make legacy-etl-gen-data NS=cnvingest; make legacy-etl-run JOB=sftp_ingest_poll)

acceptance_checks.description: Every CUSTBILL*.dat landed in the drop area is staged to incoming/ byte-identical (sha256 equal to the golden baseline for the deterministic NS=cnvingest seed).
Files become visible in incoming/ only via rename-into-place from a hidden staging path; no half-written file is ever readable under incoming/. Retires the legacy 1s size-settle hack.

A source file is deleted from the drop area only after staging, archiving, and bronze registration succeed; on any failure the drop file is left in place and the run fails loudly (no 2>/dev/null || true suppression).
Each staged file is archived under archive/<name>.<sha256[:16]> — deterministic id, no embedded timestamp, rerun-safe.

Each staged file is registered in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_ingest_files_cnvingest (one row per (ns, file_name, sha256)) and its raw lines in ow_tp.bronze.custbill_raw_cnvingest, counts recomputed from the platform.
Files not matching CUSTBILL*.dat (e.g. *.filepart, other names) are left untouched in the drop area, matching the legacy glob.
Re-running with an empty drop is a no-op; re-landing a byte-identical file re-stages it without duplicating bronze rows (MERGE keyed on ns, file_name, sha256).
All paths are derived from the ns job parameter; no hostname if-blocks, no lock files (mutual exclusion via max_concurrent_runs=1).

encoding_policy.input_encoding: unknown mainframe extract, treated as opaque bytes
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: transport is byte-transparent end-to-end: files are staged and archived as raw bytes and sha256-verified; raw lines are stored decoded as latin-1 (a lossless 1:1 byte-to-codepoint mapping) so no input byte can cause a decode failure
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: cannot occur: latin-1 maps every byte; no utf-8 decode is attempted anywhere in the chain

malformed_record_policy.details: This unit is transport-only and byte-transparent, mirroring the legacy ksh job which never inspects file contents. Record-level validation (field slicing, dates, amounts, trailer reconciliation) is owned by the parse_custbill_fixedwidth unit. Raw lines are attributed verbatim to (ns, file_name, sha256, line_no); nothing is dropped and nothing can fail open into a plausible-looking parsed row because this unit produces no parsed rows.

empty_input_semantics.details: An empty drop directory leaves incoming/, archive/ and both bronze tables exactly as they were (verified by rerun); matches legacy behaviour where the glob simply matches nothing.

planted_anomalies.description: A file not matching CUSTBILL*.dat planted in the drop area must NOT be staged, archived, registered, or deleted.
An in-flight transfer artifact (CUSTBILL_*.dat.filepart) planted in the drop area must NOT be staged; atomic rename-into-place replaces the legacy size-settle heuristic.
Invalid calendar dates, non-numeric amounts, and trailer count mismatches inside CUSTBILL files.
planted_anomalies.reason: The legacy ingest job is byte-transparent and never inspects file contents; content anomalies are detected by the parse_custbill_fixedwidth unit downstream. This unit guarantees only byte-identical transport of those anomalies into bronze raw.
